title: bindings
summary: Benilla runs every rebindable input through one chord->command engine: canonical ALT-CTRL-SHIFT chords with the exact-modifier match law, Held latches released on the base key (chat focus clears latches without eating the release), a capture seam in the options page, and account + per-character persistence files. MSUI has a real keybindings system - a rebindable table (movement, targeting, interface panels, 12+24 action-bar buttons) with primary/secondary slots, a capture UI with unbind and reset-to-defaults, and JSON persistence with legacy-schema migration - but it binds bare keys only.

openItems.text: No modifier chords: BindingPair holds bare Silk Key values - SHIFT-/CTRL-/ALT- combinations cannot be bound, and there is no exact-modifier-match rule distinguishing a bare binding from a chorded one.
No per-character binding set: one keybindings.json for everything; the reference's account-vs-character split (and the confirmed switch that deletes the character file) has no counterpart.
Rebindable command coverage is narrower than the reference's engine-wide set (e.g. chat open, autorun, camera zoom are not in the BindingRows table).
